title: Scientific Tools
text:
1. MSigDF Package

MSigDF: Molecular Signatures Database in Tidy Format




MSigDF Logo


An up-to-date fork of the Molecular Signatures Database (MSigDB) into a tibble format originally created by Stephen Turner, this updated version is up to date with MSigDB 2025.1 .
Applications: Gene set enrichment analysis - Pathway analysis - Functional genomics research - Bioinformatics workflows
Tech Stack: R, tidyverse, bioinformatics, tidy-data, msigdb
Vignette View on GitHub



2. PubMatrixR Package

PubMatrixR: Systematic Literature Search

(PubMatrixR) is an R package that performs systematic literature searches on PubMed and PMC databases using pairwise combinations of search terms. It creates co-occurrence matrices showing the number of publications that mention both terms from two different sets, enabling researchers to explore relationships between genes, diseases, pathways.



PubMatrix Logo


Applications: Biomedical Data Exploration
Now available on CRAN.
Based on paper : PubMatrix: a tool for multiplex literature mining of Becker KG et al. BMC Bioinformatics. 2003 Dec 10;4:61. doi: 10.1186/1471-2105-4-61
First forked from: https://github.com/tslaird/PubMatrixR
Vignette View on GitHub CRAN ShinyApp



3. Blind Rename Files

Blind Rename Files Swift macOS App & Bash Scripts

Rename files on folder for manual image blind analysis to avoid bias.

A swift OSX app or a bash-script to rename file, thinking in avoiding bias in manual image quantification. From the times I was doing this with ImageJ/Fiji.
Applications: Semi-automatic/manual image quantification.
View on Github Documentation

Computational Biology + Systems Biology + Genomics are my principles.

Always keeping a foot in academic collaborations - papers, student internships and rotations, supervision… et al.

title: Projects
text:
Hardware

ESP32 DuckDNS Client

Microcontroller dynDNS client with an ESP32



DuckDNS Logo


This project is an open-source, standalone Dynamic DNS (DDNS) client for DuckDNS.org that runs on an ESP32 microcontroller. This enhanced version is a complete overhaul, offering a robust, feature-rich, and secure solution to keep your DuckDNS domain pointed to your home’s dynamic IP address.
Why?… because I can.
Github Project



NTP & GPS Home Bridge

NTP and GPS monitoring systems for Home Assistant integration on Raspberry Pi.




Logo


API for GPS and NTP server. Designed to be feed into Home Assistant
Project View on Github

Looking for time and space to make more of these plans a reality.

title: Projects
text:
Home Assistant add-ons

Manyfold

Manyfold on Home Assistant



Manyfold Logo


A Home Assistant OS add-on that runs Manyfold, a self-hosted 3D model manager, with persistent storage and configurable host-backed media paths. No external PostgreSQL or Redis required.
Features: - Runs on port 3214 - Persists app data, database, and settings under /config - Configurable library and thumbnails paths on HA host storage - Supports amd64 and aarch64 - Multiuser mode toggle
View on GitHub



BentoPDF

BentoPDF on Home Assistant



BentoPDF Logo


A Home Assistant OS add-on that packages BentoPDF — a privacy-first, client-side PDF toolkit with 50+ tools. All PDF processing happens in the browser; files never leave your device.
Features: - 50+ PDF tools: merge, split, compress, convert, OCR, sign, redact - Fully client-side — no data sent to any server - HTTPS on port 8443 (enables LibreOffice WASM for office file conversion) - Supports amd64 and aarch64
View on GitHub



Zigbee ZHA Mesh Graph Export

Making a graph from a Zigbee mesh network




Logo


Export ZHA devices and neighbor edges from Home Assistant to CSV files.
Applications: none, but nerd out about the mesh made by zigbee devices using igraph, cytoscape, gephi or any other software for networks/graph analysis.
Tech Stack: Home Assistant, mesh network, graph
View on GitHub

title: Projects
text:
Creative & generative tools

Field Generation

Generative Art Through Flow Fields
Transform mathematical fields into visual harmony. This tool uses flowing patterns to guide virtual particles across your canvas, creating organic curves and paths that feel both natural and otherworldly. Nothing very original in here but at least was fun and allows the integration of other tools






Black & white flow field visualization





Features: - Export as SVG for pen plotters and laser cutters - Save as JSON/CSV for further manipulation - Real-time parameter adjustment
View Project Github



STL Shaper

Real-Time 3D Model Deformation
A playground for 3D experimentation. Apply noise, sine waves, and pixelation effects to STL models in real-time using Three.js.



Deformed Millennium Falcon model showing creative distortion effects


Capabilities: - Live deformation preview - Multiple effect layers - Noise and wave transformations - Export modified meshes - Interactive 3D manipulation
Documentation Test Project Github



Parametric Designs openSCAD


Collection of designs made with Open Scad for parametric 3D printing.


 Thingiverse Profile



XKCD - ggplot2 theme

Themes of XKCD for ggplot2




Penguins Data with XKCD Theme


An R package for creating hand-drawn, XKCD-style plots and graphics using ggplot2. Features custom geoms for jittered lines, segments, circles, and figures with the distinctive XKCD aesthetic.
Vignette View on Github

title: Projects
text:
Utilities & scripts

Ollama Chat History Cleaner

Clean Ollama Chat History and Logs
Scripts to clean only the chat history and logs from Ollama GUI and server. Does not remove models, users, or app settings. Solves the gap in Ollama’s native chat history deletion.
Features: - Delete chat history from Ollama database - Delete Ollama logs - Automatic database path detection (macOS/Windows) - Optional backup before deletion - Cross-platform support: macOS, Linux, Windows
View Project View on GitHub

title: Site Organization Suggestions — toledoem.github.io
text:
The site has two very different audiences and two very different kinds of content — yet the nav treats everything as a flat list of roughly equal weight. You are a scientist-engineer-artist, but someone landing on the site cannot tell that in five seconds. The current top-level sections are:

About Me · Hardware & Code · Scientific Tools · Projects Details (dropdown) · Gallery · Papers

“Hardware & Code” and “Scientific Tools” are artificial distinctions. STLShaper is hardware-adjacent and creative. PubMatrixR is scientific but also a software package. The XKCD theme is code but for science. The current split does not hold up.




Eight items are buried in a dropdown named Projects Details (grammatically awkward), with no hierarchy or grouping. The items range from full R packages with vignettes (MSigDF, PubMatrixR, xkcd) to firmware (ESP32 DuckDNS) to a bash script (Blind Rename) to a creative web tool (STLShaper). These are very different things dumped in one bucket.




The sitemap reveals pages with no path from the main nav:







Orphaned page
URL




BrandSTL
/BrandSTL/index.html


PubMatrixR Python port
/pubmatrixp/index.html


Static Site Image Optimizer
/StaticSiteImageOptimizer/index.html


Field generation — triangle fields
/field_generation/triangle-fields/index.html


Field generation — math docs
/field_generation/doc/field_generation_math.html



These exist, are indexed by search engines, but are unreachable from any navigation link.




gallery.html and image.html are essentially the same page — same images, slightly different wording — with image.html carrying a 2025 lastmod date and an older Quarto version. One is a ghost that should be consolidated or retired.




/NTPGPSHomeBridge/msigdf/ is an old copy of the msigdf pkgdown site that was deployed inside the NTPGPSHomeBridge directory. It is present in the sitemap, which means search engines index it as duplicate content under a confusing URL. It should be deleted.




Some projects get a full pkgdown sub-site with reference docs and vignettes (MSigDF, PubMatrixR, xkcd). Some get a section on a shared page (Ollama Cleaner, Zigbee Mesh, Manyfold HA). Some get their own standalone app page (STLShaper, Field Generation). There is no consistent pattern, so visitors do not know what depth of content awaits them when they click something.




15+ publications spanning 2015–2026 across genomics, neurobiology, cardio-metabolism, and bioinformatics are listed as a single unscannable block. There is no way to filter by year, topic, or authorship role (first author vs. co-author).




The Mermaid diagram (Science → Biomedicine, Data Science, etc.) renders as raw text in some contexts, and it sits between the bio and a photo without a clear purpose. The page conflates a personal introduction with a career summary with a concept map — three things that each deserve their own space or treatment.





Stripping away the current page names, your content naturally falls into five groups:







Group
What belongs here




Identity
Who you are, career arc, connect links


Research
Publications, your role in each, field context


Bioinformatics software
MSigDF, PubMatrixR (+ Shiny app), xkcd ggplot2, Bash Blind Rename


Engineering & utilities
ESP32 DuckDNS, NTPGPSHomeBridge, Zigbee Mesh, Manyfold HA, BentoPDF HA, Ollama Cleaner, StaticSiteImageOptimizer


Creative & generative
STLShaper, Field Generation (all variants), generative art gallery, OpenSCAD/parametric designs, BrandSTL







Home
Research
  └── Papers
Software
  ├── Bioinformatics tools
  │     ├── MSigDF
  │     ├── PubMatrixR  →  [sub-site]
  │     ├── xkcd ggplot2 theme  →  [sub-site]
  │     └── Bash Blind Rename
  └── Engineering & utilities
        ├── ESP32 DuckDNS
        ├── NTP GPS HomeBridge
        ├── Zigbee Mesh Export
        ├── Manyfold HA add-on
        ├── BentoPDF HA add-on
        ├── Ollama Chat Cleaner
        └── Static Site Image Optimizer
Creative
  ├── STLShaper  →  [sub-site]
  ├── Field Generation  →  [app + triangle fields + math docs]
  ├── BrandSTL
  └── Gallery  (consolidates gallery.html + image.html)
About







Delete /NTPGPSHomeBridge/msigdf/ — stale duplicate, confuses search engines.
Retire image.html — redirect or remove; keep only gallery.html.
Rename “Projects Details” to something grammatically correct (“Projects” is fine).
Surface pubmatrixp, BrandSTL, and StaticSiteImageOptimizer with at least a card on the relevant page.





Split the nav into the five groups above. The dropdown pattern is fine; the contents of the dropdown need to be grouped and labelled, not listed as a flat sequence.
Add authorship context to Papers — a simple badge or annotation per paper showing whether you are first author, co-author, or corresponding author goes a long way for a non-specialist reader.
Link the full field generation content — triangle fields and the math documentation page are both unreachable from the nav.





Collapse “Hardware & Code” and “Scientific Tools” into a single “Software” section with internal grouping. The current split forces artificial decisions (where does the XKCD R package go? It is scientific, it is code, it is creative).
Give the About page a single job — personal introduction only. Move the career summary to a dedicated CV or Research page, and either fix the Mermaid diagram or remove it.
Standardise project entry points — decide on one of: (a) card on a parent page + link to sub-site, or (b) standalone page. Mixing both without a pattern makes the site feel unfinished.
